title: Ride-hailing
summary: Live driver locations in an in-memory geo index, sharded by area.

lesson.problem: Hundreds of thousands of drivers report their position every few seconds, and each ride request must find the nearest available drivers in milliseconds.
why: Location updates are a firehose of writes (1 million drivers every 4 seconds is 250,000 writes per second), and only the latest position matters. So they live in memory, not in a relational database.
To answer "who is near me?" quickly, the map is divided into cells (geohash, S2 or H3). Drivers are indexed by cell, and a search only looks at the rider's cell and its neighbours.
The index is sharded by geography, so one city's traffic lands on one shard. The shard router maps a cell to its shard. Busy areas get smaller cells or their own shards.
takeaways: Shard by the key your queries use: here, location.
Expect hot spots (city centres, stadiums) and split them further.
Riders near a shard boundary need results from neighbouring cells too.
